title: flora workflow
description: A named, versioned execution contract: which steps run, on which harness, and what proves each step is done. The verifier runs the checks itself; the next step is not released until the current contract is closed.

name.description: Workflow name. Shows up in the journal, `flora runs` and the viewer.

version.description: Contract version, for your own bookkeeping.

description.description: One line on what the workflow does — shown by `flora inspect` and `flora workflows` when the workflow travels as a bundle.

params.description: Input parameters. Passed with `flora run … --param name=value`; substitute `{{name}}` (or `{{params.name}}`) in prompts, commands and checks.

steps.description: Executed in order. A step runs only after the previous one passed its verification.

trigger.description: Triggers for `flora watch`: a cron schedule and/or polled sources. The event is reachable as {{event.*}} in prompts and check expectations and as `.event` in $FLORA_CONTEXT (never inside a shell line).

cron.description: Five fields, local time: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. `*`, `*/n`, `a-b`, `a,b,c`. Missed ticks while the machine slept are not caught up.

sentry_source.description: Polls Sentry's issue list; every new matching issue id starts one run. The token comes from $SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, never from the file.

match.description: Regular expression the issue title or culprit must match.

interval_sec.description: Poll interval (default 60). Errors back off exponentially up to 15 minutes.

url.description: API host for self-hosted installs (default https://sentry.io).

command_source.description: Polls by running a command: a JSON object per stdout line is one event each (its `id` is the dedup key), plain text is one event, empty output is silence.

required.description: Refuse to run when the value is missing.

default.description: Used when no value is passed.

description.description: What to pass — shown by `flora inspect`.

id.description: Unique within the workflow. Later steps reference this step's output as `{{steps.<id>.output…}}`, so it must be a plain identifier.

title.description: Human-readable label for the CLI and the viewer.

needs.description: Steps this one waits for — ids declared earlier in the file. Without it a step waits for the one right above it. Steps whose needs are met run at the same time (up to FLORA_MAX_PARALLEL).

when.description: Run only if this holds after {{…}} substitution: `A == B`, `A != B`, `A` (truthy), `!A`. Otherwise the step is skipped and its dependants go on. `{{steps.<id>.status}}` is available.

prompt.description: Task text for a harness executor (claude-code, codex, antigravity). Placeholders: `{{params.*}}`, `{{steps.<id>.output…}}`.

run.description: Shell command for the `command` executor. `{{params.*}}` is allowed; `{{steps.*}}` is not — a shell step reads earlier outputs from the JSON file at $FLORA_CONTEXT.

verify.description: Verification contract. The step passes only when every check passes; the verifier runs them, never the executor.

verify_in.description: Where the checks run. `cwd` (default): the run directory as the executor left it. `worktree`: a fresh detached worktree of HEAD — only what the executor committed can pass. Needs a git repository.

retry.description: Extra attempts after a failure. A retry after a broken output contract tells the agent what was wrong.

tools.description: Tools mounted into the harness for this step, and nothing beyond them: external MCP servers plus the flora-native `read_context` and `call_workflow`. Only claude-code and codex can mount tools.

parallel.description: Fan-out: the branches run at the same time (at most FLORA_MAX_PARALLEL, default 3), each in its own git worktree of HEAD, and `require` decides whether the step passed. Later steps read `{{steps.<id>.outputs}}` (one entry per branch, null where it failed) and `{{steps.<id>.patches}}`.

require.description: How many branches must pass: `all` (default), `any`, or `quorum:N`.

isolation.description: `worktree` (default): every branch in a detached worktree of HEAD, its changes handed back as a patch; needs a git repository. `shared`: all branches in the run directory, no patches.

branch.description: One branch of a parallel step: a step body without an id (it becomes `<step>[i]`), retries or nesting.

tool.description: One tool source: `{ mcp: { name, command, args, env } }` starts an MCP server for the step; `{ flora: call_workflow, workflow }` lets the agent run another workflow and get its verdict; `{ flora: read_context }` lets it read this run's params and step outputs.

name.description: Server name; the harness sees its tools as mcp__<name>__<tool>. `flora` is reserved for the built-in tools.

env.description: Environment for the server process. Values may use {{params.*}}; secrets belong in params or the environment, not in the file.

workflow.description: Workflow file the agent may run, relative to the step's working directory.

harness.description: Which adapter executes the step: `claude-code` (claude -p), `codex` (codex exec), `antigravity` (agy --print, Gemini models), `command` (a shell command) or `api` (one prompt → one completion from a model API named by `provider` and configured in ~/.flora/providers.yaml — never a default).

model.description: Model passed through to the harness.

provider.description: `api` harness: the provider's name in ~/.flora/providers.yaml (where the request goes, which environment variable holds the key).

reasoning.description: `antigravity` harness: reasoning level, appended to the model id (`gemini-4-carbon` + `high` → `gemini-4-carbon-high`). Default `medium` when the model is a family.

access.description: `antigravity` harness: `read` (default) — the agent may only read the run directory: no commands, file writes, network or MCP; `write` — it may edit the workspace, commands run in the terminal sandbox.

timeout_min.description: Wall-clock ceiling in minutes (default 15, 0 disables). Exceeding it kills the whole process tree.

stall_min.description: Silence ceiling in minutes (default 5, 0 disables): no output for this long counts as a hang and the process tree is killed.

args.description: Extra CLI arguments passed through to the harness.

type.description: `command`: run a shell command and judge its exit code / output. `artifact`: a file must exist (and contain a string).

run.description: command: the shell command. `{{steps.*}}` is not allowed here either; read $FLORA_CONTEXT.

expect_match.description: command: substring that must appear in the check's output. Placeholders allowed, including `{{steps.*}}`.

path.description: artifact: path that must exist, relative to the run's working directory.

contains.description: artifact: substring the file must contain. Placeholders allowed, including `{{steps.*}}`.

output.description: Output contract: what the step hands to the steps after it. The value is journaled as `StepResult.output` and reachable as `{{steps.<id>.output…}}` and in $FLORA_CONTEXT.

type.description: `json`: a command's output is parsed as JSON; an agent is asked to end with one ```json block and the last valid block is taken. `text` (default): kept as is. Either way the value is capped at 256KB.

schema.description: JSON Schema the parsed value must satisfy (needs `type: json`). A mismatch fails the step with the reason.

output_repair.description: Output repair: when an agent's answer breaks the JSON output contract (not JSON, no block, empty, or not matching the schema), flora asks the same agent — in its own session when the harness can resume it (claude-code, codex, antigravity), otherwise once with a new short request — to return the same result in the required form, read-only, before failing the step. At the workflow root it is the default for every agent step; on a parallel step, for its branches. Agent harnesses with `output.type: json` only.

attempts.description: Repair requests per step attempt before the step fails (default 2). 0 turns repair off: a broken contract fails the step at once.

timeout_min.description: Wall-clock ceiling of one repair request in minutes (default 5), never longer than the step's executor.timeout_min. 0 leaves only the executor's limit.
